title: Mask Adoption Behavior Simulation
description: Simulate how mask-wearing behavior spreads and persists in a population under social influence, information campaigns, availability, and policy mandates.

interactions.name: social_influence
interactions.description: People observe contacts' mask use; higher neighbor adoption increases an individual's probability to adopt (conformity) and updates perceived norms.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations apply mandates; non-compliant persons face denial of entry or penalties based on enforcement level.

interactions.name: information_dissemination
interactions.description: Media channels and policy announcements alter risk perception, trust, and adoption propensity; misinformation reduces adoption or trust.

interactions.name: mask_purchase
interactions.description: Persons buy masks from retailers subject to stock, price, and rationing; inventory affects ability to comply.

interactions.name: movement_and_exposure
interactions.description: Persons move among locations (home, work, public); context-specific policies and norms shape compliance in situ.

interactions.name: household_norm_transmission
interactions.description: Households align members' norms and share resources, influencing adoption coherence within the household.

metrics.name: overall_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of people wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent
metrics.description: Number of days to reach 50% adoption.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum adoption rate achieved during the simulation.

metrics.name: sustained_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Average adoption rate after a specified day or after mandate removal.

metrics.name: violation_rate
metrics.description: Share of visits to locations where persons are non-compliant under an active policy.

metrics.name: policy_effect_size
metrics.description: Difference-in-differences of adoption before vs. after mandate controlling for trend.

metrics.name: network_influence_index
metrics.description: Correlation between neighbor adoption and individual adoption probability.

metrics.name: stockout_frequency
metrics.description: Fraction of days retailers have zero stock.

metrics.name: adoption_inequality
metrics.description: Disparity in adoption across income or household SES (e.g., Gini or Theil index).

validation_criteria.name: s_curve_adoption
validation_criteria.description: In baseline with social influence, the cumulative adoption trajectory should exhibit an S-shaped curve.

validation_criteria.name: monotonic_policy_response
validation_criteria.description: Increasing enforcement_probability or penalty_amount should not decrease adoption when other parameters are fixed.

validation_criteria.name: no_influence_sanity_check
validation_criteria.description: With social_influence_weight=0, messaging_intensity=0, and no mandate, adoption should remain near the initial_adoption_rate absent inventory changes.

validation_criteria.name: stock_dependency
validation_criteria.description: If retailer stock and restock are set to zero, adoption cannot exceed initial_adoption_rate plus existing mask_inventory.
